propositions: On platforms without /proc (macOS), _process_start_time always returns None, making the recycled-pid discriminator unsatisfiable and causing dead holders whose pid was recycled by unrelated live processes to never be reclaimed, resulting in unbounded lock wedging.
When current_start is None (unavailable start time), the live-pid verdict is unqualified and should fall back to the 1h ceiling timeout rather than skipping the reclamation check entirely.
A genuinely live owner cannot reach the staleness check because it holds the exclusive fcntl leg for the entire lifetime of the mkdir leg, so applying the ceiling only fires on orphaned locks.

The owner-identity and lock reclamation logic was split from lock.py (798 LOC) into lock_owner.py to stay within the 800 LOC module size limit, with lock.py reaching moved names module-qualified to avoid creating duplicate bindings that would break monkeypatching.
